conventions.convention: A finite source has m ≥ 1 and strictly positive probabilities summing to one. Product blocks have length n ≥ 1 and are ordered lexicographically.
Codewords are nonempty. Unique decodability means injectivity of the extension on all finite source words, including comparisons between different source lengths.
A prefix code must be nonsingular as well as having no proper-prefix relation between distinct codewords.
H₂(p) = H(p)/ln 2; H(p) uses natural logarithms, while code lengths and H₂ use bits.
Huffman ties use increasing serial numbers; the first removed node is the left child, labeled 0. A singleton receives codeword 0.

Ideal-real coding uses half-open source intervals and the midpoint dyadic cell of length floor(−log₂ w)+2. The decoder knows the source and fixed block length; streams have an externally known frame count.

Finite-register coding requires positive integer frequencies, a public cap N, fixed 1 ≤ n ≤ N, and an outer frame count R. B is the least nonnegative integer with Q^N ≤ 2^B; register widths depend on this configuration.

load_bearing.statement: For a finite list of positive integers ℓ₁,…,ℓₘ, there is a binary prefix code on [m] having codeword lengths ℓᵢ if and only if ∑ᵢ2^(−ℓᵢ) ≤ 1.
Let C be a finite binary uniquely decodable code with lengths ℓᵢ. Then ∑ᵢ2^(−ℓᵢ) ≤ 1.
Let p and q be probability vectors with qᵢ > 0 for every i. Then D(p||q) ≥ 0, with equality if and only if p = q.

For a finite full-support source p, every finite binary uniquely decodable code satisfies Lₚ(C) ≥ H₂(p). If m ≥ 2, prefix lengths ⌈−log₂ pᵢ⌉ have expected length strictly less than H₂(p)+1. If m = 1, codeword 0 has length 1 = H₂(p)+1.

For every finite full-support source, the deterministic Huffman algorithm terminates, returns a binary prefix code, and minimizes expected length among binary prefix codes on the same alphabet. Its singleton codeword 0 is optimal among nonempty codewords.

For fixed p and n, the ideal-real code is injective and prefix-free on the block alphabet, with length at most −log₂ pⁿ(xⁿ)+2; blocks are recovered uniquely and concatenated fixed-length-block frames are uniquely parsed.

For every configured rational model and fixed frame length, the codebook assigns distinct prefix-free words with lengths at most B+2 and −log₂ pⁿ(xⁿ)+2. The decoder returns the encoded block, configuration and searches terminate, and the stated per-frame registers do not overflow.
